title: ADJUDICATE: GUARD_PPM 250 (spec 02a 2a.6) vs 5000 (all code + vectors) - which is authoritative
description: Child of b7z9.25 (R-02a-082 timing params): spec 02a-coordinated-capacity.md says GUARD_PPM = 250, but every code path (python/src/lichen/timing/ccp7.py:11) and every vector (ccp7_holdover.json, ccp16-desync.json excessive_clock_drift_desync) uses 5000; Rust lacks the TIMEOUT/REJOIN constants entirely. This is a spec-vs-implementation conflict requiring Mark's adjudication: either the spec constant is wrong (fix spec 02a to 5000 and keep code) or the implementations are wrong (change to 250 - would break the existing vectors). Human decision; do not pick silently.
close_reason: RESOLVED - SPEC ALREADY CORRECT: the bead's premise ('spec says GUARD_PPM = 250') is wrong. Verified at spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md:285: 'GUARD_PPM | 5000 | Maximum tolerable clock drift (parts per million). Conservative default for low-cost LoRa oscillators' — and the transition table (:268) references GUARD_PPM generically with no other numeric value. There is no 250 anywhere in the spec (grep confirmed). All code (python ccp7.py GUARD_PPM=5000, sfn.py DESYNC_CONSTANTS GUARD_PPM=5000) and vectors (ccp16-desync excessive_clock_drift_desync guard_ppm=5000) match the spec exactly. No conflict exists; no adjudication needed. The only genuine remaining item in this family is the Rust TIMEOUT/REJOIN constants (noted in the original description) — but Rust takes guard_ppm as a function parameter (on_drift(drift_ppm, guard_ppm)), so the constants live at the call site, which is an integration-layer concern (d7hg), not a spec conflict.
